name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican Tom Sell's large fundraising and outside support edge
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Prediction markets price Republican win near 98%
model.rationale: This West Texas seat carries a heavy Republican lean, and the open-seat dynamic does little to change it. Sell has raised over $2.1 million with substantial outside backing while Democrat Rable has raised about $31,000, and markets price the race as all but decided for Republicans.
model.watch: A major late scandal or unexpected outside spending surge for the Democrat is essentially the only path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-19 is a deeply Republican West Texas district, and with Jodey Arrington retiring the seat remains strongly favored to stay in Republican hands. The fundamentals point to a roughly twenty-point Republican margin, consistent with the district's partisan lean and a favorable national environment for the party.

Republican Tom Sell has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from more than $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 98 percent chance. No polls or expert ratings are available, but the financial and structural evidence leaves little doubt about the expected outcome.
